take_homes: The model's report on its own work is a claim, not a result. Have an independent reader or my own judgment check it.
What the agent learns can be saved in a plain text file that the next session reads. That is something the company would own, unlike a licence.
Before an agent writes several files, make it show a plan and approve it first.

monday.move: Ask my controller to try the month-end variance commentary with an agent, using one closed month where we already know the answer.
monday.when: Next month-end close, as a side-by-side trial
monday.stop_condition: Stop if the draft needs more than 30 minutes of correction, or if it states a number that is not in the source data.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data. Until it does, only anonymised or old data can be used.

misconception.why: The rules file that the next session reads shows that the learning is saved in something the organisation holds, not in the tool I bought. I still think of AI as a licence first, because the module gave no cost, adoption or payback figure.

one_line: Three or four good ideas about checking the model's own work, buried under a personal website exercise and the same filler paragraph pasted in a dozen times. I'd have liked one cost-and-payback number.
